We've seen plenty of reports about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced it has completed the first surgical procedure using an innovative app on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, performed using the SportSuite Vision app, which brings "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." This includes arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT imaging.

Here's Stryker's description of the app:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to view both physical objects and digital tools simultaneously in the operating room, such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT imaging. During arthroscopic surgery, surgeons often need to rely on multiple displays in the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology reduces reliance on traditional monitors and supports a more streamlined, ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker says this makes it the first app authorized by the FDA for intraoperative use on Vision Pro.
